VBO:0201128.summary: Lively and cheerful, the Ratonero Murciano is sociable with familiar people and strongly attached to its owner. It can be energetic and determined while watching the household, then peaceful and self-assured at rest. This small rural dog was used against vermin in Murcia’s granaries; local breed work has sought to preserve the scattered population as the region’s economy changed.
VBO:0201128.shortDescription: A lively, owner-attached Murcian ratter, energetic while watching its household and more peaceful when at rest.

sources.title: ACCAM — Ratonero Murciano standard
sources.evidence: Defines lively cheerful owner-faithful rural vermin/granary/guard/companion roles and declining dispersed population as rural economy changed. Literal natural long tail never reaches hock, customary docking noted but not required. Child-suitability statement excluded.

sources.title: ACCAM — Phenotypic and morphological study of Ratonero Murciano
sources.evidence: Original rural vermin roles and recovery work since1997. Normative appendix describes lively cheerful social/owner-attached dog, energetic determined guard work then peaceful/self-assured at rest. Study explicitly distinguishes Mallorqui/Valencian and identifies black-tan photograph. Ancient/English-ship origin speculation, nutritional causality, congenital-anury percentages/genetic claims and medical exclusions omitted from profile.

VBO:0008018.summary: Closely bonded to its owner, the Iletsua has a pronounced territorial streak in its breed standard. It is the rough-coated variety of the Basque herding dog, alongside Gorbeiakoa. Local conservation work seeks to preserve both forms of the Euskal Artzain Txakurra.
VBO:0008018.shortDescription: An owner-bonded Basque herding variety with a pronounced territorial streak, described in its own Iletsua standard.

sources.title: EATA — Iletsua variety standard
sources.evidence: Exact Iletsua character describes close owner bond/faithfulness and marked territoriality. Separate morphological standard distinguishes rough blond/fawn/cinnamon form from Gorbeiakoa. Association defines/preserves both varieties of the Basque shepherd; no child suitability, intelligence, parent temperament or FCI recognition claim.

sources.title: EATA — Iletsua photographic standard plate
sources.evidence: Whole exact titled Euskal Artzain Txakurra Iletsua plate identifies Perro de pastoreo and shows developed rough-coated adult-looking body/head, medium folded triangular ears, strong limbs and tail plume. Head proportion diagram5/5 conflicts with literal text5/4; neither numerical ratio used in synthesis.
